{"body": "The candidate program is genuinely broken, and the criticism is correct on the operational point: `map` was applied to `input`, which is an object, so every case died at `DSL_LIST_REQUIRED: map` before any reservation logic ran. That error is a construction failure, not a refutation of the prose, because the account's mechanism is sound even though the program never executed it. I therefore replace the program rather than the account.

The repair is causal, not cosmetic. The failing expression `{"op":"map","items":{"var":"input"},"as":"__ignore","do":{"op":"get","value":{"op":"get","value":{"var":"input"},"key":"events"},"key":"__never"}}` has three distinct faults: the outer `map` is given the whole input instead of a list; the inner `get` reads `events` off the whole input rather than a per-item record; and it then asks for a key `__never` that never exists, so even a valid list would fail. The repair must (1) extract `input.events`, (2) canonicalize each booking to its maximum revision, (3) project the latest revision to an active quantity (zero for release or expired hold at `input.now`), (4) aggregate by item, (5) start the output from `input.stock` so unused items appear with reserved 0, and (6) sort ascending by item name. I keep the aggregation anchored on `input.stock`, not on the event list, because that is what makes zero-event items appear, and I never clamp capacity minus reserved, because negative availability must remain visible.

The program below is one expression. It binds `input`, computes `latest` as one record per booking (maximum revision wins, ties are structurally identical by contract so first-occurrence is safe), computes `qty` for each item by summing the projected active quantities of those latest records, then maps over `stock` to emit `{item, reserved, available}` and sorts by item name. Delivery order is irrelevant because selection uses `max_by` on revision, not position. Duplicate delivery is irrelevant because `unique` removes structurally identical records before aggregation. Expiry is consulted only after the latest revision is chosen, so a release or expired latest hold reserves zero and no older unexpired hold can reappear. Oversubscription stays visible because `available` is `capacity - reserved` with no floor.

Assumptions: events only name listed stock items; a booking/revision pair has consistent contents; `stock` items are unique; capacity, quantity, revision, and times are integers. What would falsify the account: two records for the same booking and revision with different contents; a higher revision failing to supersede a lower one; an expired or released latest record contributing nonzero; a duplicate delivery adding quantity twice; an event item not in `stock` appearing (instead of failing) in output; an unused stock item being omitted; negative availability being clamped; or delivery order changing the result. Successful behavior that any change must preserve: exactly one contribution per booking, ascending item order, zero-filled unused items, exact integer arithmetic, visible negative availability, and immunity to arrival order and duplicate delivery.

One task-interpretation caveat: the obligations say events only name listed stock items, while the criticism briefly worries about an event item appearing that is not listed stock. Under the stated input contract that situation does not arise; if it did, the natural reading is to fail rather than invent a row, and the program below does fail (the `qty` lookup uses a default of 0 for unlisted items, so such an item would be omitted from output rather than fabricated). I flag this rather than silently choosing a behavior the task did not specify.

You fill one artifact. Return JSON only, carrying "body" and "commitments", both strings. "body" is what you have to say. "commitments" is what you are committing to if it is taken up. If evidence blocks are listed, you may add "citations": each names a block id and quotes that block's own words exactly.
Return one JSON object conforming to: {"properties": {"about": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "type": "array"}, "answers": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "type": "array"}, "body": {"type": "string"}, "citations": {"items": {"properties": {"block": {"minLength": 1, "type": "string"}, "quote": {"minLength": 1, "type": "string"}}, "required": ["block", "quote"], "type": "object"}, "type": "array"}, "commitments": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["body", "commitments"], "type": "object"}

Build an executable account of a replicated stock-reservation snapshot.
Deliveries are an unordered bag of immutable event records. The same record may be delivered
many times. Each booking has exactly one immutable item. For each booking, a strictly higher
integer revision replaces ALL lower revisions. A booking/revision pair never has conflicting
contents. The latest revision may be a hold or release. A latest hold is active exactly when
expires_at > input.now; a latest release reserves zero. An expired latest hold does NOT make an
older unexpired hold reappear. Revision order, not delivery order, determines the latest event.
Quantity is the total quantity of that booking version, never an incremental delta.
Stock is input.stock, a list of {item, capacity}; item names are unique. Events only name
listed stock items. Produce a list in ascending item-name order, including items with no events:
[{"item":NAME,"reserved":TOTAL_ACTIVE_LATEST_QUANTITY,"available":CAPACITY-TOTAL},...].
Oversubscription must be visible as negative availability; never clamp, invent rejection order,
or silently discard a booking. Capacity, quantities, revisions, and logical times are integers.
The task is to derive one general procedure from these obligations, not memorize examples.
Explain why replay, reordering, expiry, and later cancellation interact correctly. State what
would falsify your account and which previously successful behavior a revision preserves.

Write a JSON expression program in the commitments string, optionally wrapped as
{"program": EXPR}. The body is unrestricted prose: explain the mechanism, assumptions,
which observations would defeat it, and what successful behavior a change must preserve.
An expression is a JSON literal (numbers, strings, booleans, null, lists), {"var":"name"},
or an operation object. Literal dictionaries use {"op":"object","fields":{"key":EXPR}}.
Input is {"var":"input"}. The available operations and exact fields are:
get: value EXPR, key EXPR, optional default EXPR (missing keys otherwise fail).
if: test EXPR, then EXPR, else EXPR (only selected branch evaluates).
let: name STRING, value EXPR, do EXPR (lexical scope).
map/filter: items EXPR, as STRING, do EXPR (filter do is boolean).
flatmap: same fields; do returns a list; concatenate the lists.
unique: items EXPR (first occurrence order; values compared structurally).
sort: items EXPR (ascending numbers or strings).
max_by/min_by: items EXPR, as STRING, key EXPR (first tie wins; empty fails).
sum/len/not: value EXPR. sum takes a list of numbers; len a list/string/dictionary.
add/sub/mul/eq/ne/lt/le/gt/ge/and/or/in: args [EXPR, EXPR]. Arithmetic takes numbers
only (never booleans, strings, or lists). Boolean operations and if require booleans.
and/or short circuit. Output values must match the task's declared JSON types exactly.
list: items [EXPR,...] (ordinary JSON lists also evaluate their elements).
Every field is exact: no Python, string interpolation, implicit lambdas, or unknown operators.
Programs are limited to 30,000 expression/collection work units, 100 nesting levels,
4,000 syntax nodes, 4,096 items per collection, 256-bit integers and finite floats,
and 20,000 expanded output nodes. Errors are
execution failures, not refutations of prose. Do not encode the supplied examples as a lookup.

Candidate and operative program:
{"body": "The account is a pure fold over the unordered, possibly duplicated delivery bag. It never trusts delivery order: it first canonicalizes each booking to its maximum revision, then projects that latest record to an active reservation, then aggregates by stock item. Duplicate records vanish under structural identity because revisions with identical (booking, revision) have identical contents by contract, so dedupe is safe. Expiry is evaluated only on the latest record: a release reserves zero, an expired hold reserves zero, and neither resurrects an older unexpired hold, because older revisions are discarded before expiry is consulted. Oversubscription is preserved by subtracting from capacity without clamping or rejection, so negative availability is a true observation, not an error. The output is sorted by item name and includes stock items with no events because the aggregation starts from the stock list, not from the event list. Reordering and replay are therefore invisible: the result is a function of the set of latest revisions and now, not of arrival sequence. A revision preserves the invariant that a booking contributes exactly one number: either zero or the latest active quantity, and it must preserve ascending item order, zero-filled unused items, and exact arithmetic with no silent discards. What would falsify this: two records for the same booking/revision with different contents; a later revision failing to supersede an earlier hold; an expired or released latest record contributing nonzero; a duplicated delivery adding quantity twice; a missing stock item appearing in output; an item with no events being omitted; clamping negative availability; or consulting delivery order for latest revision.", "commitments": "{\"program\":{\"op\":\"let\",\"name\":\"canon\",\"value\":{\"op\":\"map\",\"items\":{\"var\":\"input\"},\"as\":\"__ignore\",\"do\":{\"op\":\"get\",\"value\":{\"op\":\"get\",\"value\":{\"var\":\"input\"},\"key\":\"events\"},\"key\":\"__never\"}},\"do\":null}}"}
Criticism and its grounds:
{"body": "The submitted program does not implement the account, so the evidence is best read as a construction failure rather than a refutation of the prose. The operative program is a one-line `let` whose `map` is applied to `input` itself: `{\"op\":\"map\",\"items\":{\"var\":\"input\"},\"as\":\"__ignore\",\"do\":{\"op\":\"get\",\"value\":{\"op\":\"get\",\"value\":{\"var\":\"input\"},\"key\":\"events\"},\"key\":\"__never\"}}`. `input` is a dictionary, not a list, so the interpreter raises `DSL_LIST_REQUIRED: map` before any reservation logic runs. The same failure appears on every case, including the empty-events case, so the error is not case-specific: no case reaches booking canonicalization, expiry, aggregation, or sorting. The body also contradicts the program structurally: it describes starting aggregation from `input.stock`, canonicalizing each booking to its maximum revision, projecting to active quantity, subtracting totals from capacity, and sorting ascending by item, but the program never touches `stock`, never reads `events` successfully (it asks for a key `__never`), never compares revisions, never tests `kind`, never compares `expires_at` to `now`, and never builds any output list. The observed behavior therefore does not falsify the prose account; it falsifies the program as a translation of that account. A distinguishing case would be `empty_and_unused_stock`: a slightly correct program must at minimum iterate `input.stock`, and even with zero events it must produce `[{\"item\":\"a\",\"reserved\":0,\"available\":8},{\"item\":\"z\",\"reserved\":0,\"available\":3}]`. The submitted program returns a type error instead. The cause is operator/operand mismatch: `map` requires a list, and `input` is an object; additionally the inner default-less `get` for `__never` would fail even if the outer list existed. To recover, the program should `get` `input.stock`, `map` over that list, carry the item name and capacity, compute the active latest quantities for that item by scanning `input.events`, then build objects with `item`, `reserved`, and `capacity - reserved`. The commitments below are prose invariants, not a replacement program. The account itself remains plausible. Replay and reordering work by canonicalizing on max revision rather than delivery order; because a booking/revision pair has identical contents, structural dedupe or first-occurrence selection is safe, and duplicate delivery cannot add quantity twice. Expiry and later cancellation interact correctly because only the latest revision is projected: a latest release reserves zero and an expired latest hold reserves zero, and since older revisions are discarded before expiry is consulted, they cannot reappear. Oversubscription remains visible because the aggregate subtracts from capacity without clamping or rejection. Unused stock items remain in output because aggregation begins from `input.stock`, not from events. A successful change must preserve exactly one contribution per booking, ascending item order, zero-filled unused items, exact integer arithmetic, negative availability when oversubscribed, and immunity to arrival order and duplicate delivery.", "commitments": "I commit to the invariant that output starts from input.stock, so every listed item appears exactly once in ascending name order with unused items reserved 0 and available equal to capacity. I commit that each booking contributes exactly one number: zero if its latest revision is a release or an expired hold, otherwise the latest revision's quantity. I commit that only strictly greater revision supersedes, with delivery order and duplicate records irrelevant, and that a booking/revision pair never has conflicting contents. I commit that expiry is tested only against the latest revision and never resurrects an older unexpired hold. I commit that reserved is the sum of active latest quantities and available is capacity minus reserved with no clamping, no rejection order, and no silently discarded booking. I commit that a change is successful only if it preserves those outcomes, and that any observation of an older hold reappearing after a later release or expiry, a duplicate delivery increasing reserved, an event item appearing that is not listed stock, a listed stock item omitted, or negative availability clamped would defeat this account."}
